name: Thabo
dialog: The lighthouse keeper?
He didn’t leave town.
He just… stopped being seen.
He fixed my bicycle chain once. Never said a word the whole time. Best repair I ever had.

bell: First night in years I slept with the window open.
Just in case it rings again.

postQuestDialog: You found his things?
Then he was still trying to do his job.
Even after everyone else moved on.
I've heard that Hlokomela may know more.

quest.description: Recover belongings left behind by the lighthouse keeper.
quest.unlockText: The keeper never left town. Hlokomela tends what's left of the paths going up to the light.

name: Lerato
dialog: I miss the smell of rain along the cliffs.
Storms come fast, then disappear into the bay.
The coast really shows its moods here.

fragments: People say Nandi found pieces of the old bell.
She always heard the weather before the rest of us did.
Maybe some people just listen better.

name: Sipho
dialog: Nothing beats a braai by the seaside.
Everyone debates which boerewors brand is best.
As long as the fire is hot, the day’s a win.

keeper: They say the lighthouse keeper never actually left town.
Forty years, and the man never once came to a braai.
Some people keep a different kind of fire going.

name: Nomsa
dialog: The wind off the ocean is fierce.
One second calm, next your hat sails away.
Still, the view over the cliffs makes it worth it.

name: Kagiso
dialog: You’re asking about the bell?
It wasn’t for ships. It was for people.
When someone didn’t come home… it rang.
Nineteen strokes for a boat overdue. I used to count them against my window.

bell: Nineteen strokes for a boat overdue. Three for a safe return.
Somebody up there remembered the code.

postQuestDialog: I’m glad someone still listens.
Places don’t forget things.
People do.
I've heard that Thabo may know more.

quest.description: Find remnants of the town’s old emergency paths.
quest.unlockText: The old routes all lead toward the point. Thabo knew the keeper — back when there was a keeper.

name: Zanele
dialog: Local music by the waves lifts the spirit.
The rhythm makes your feet chase the shoreline.
You can’t help but move with it.

name: Musa
dialog: The beaches here are peaceful, with warm water and warmer smiles.
Just don’t forget sun protection.
The tide and the people are what make it magical.

bell: I was in the water when it rang.
Every swimmer stood up at the same time, like church.

name: Anele
dialog: Hiking the coastal cliffs clears the mind.
The cliffs make you feel small, yet part of something larger.
Adventure is all around here if you look.

name: Vusi
dialog: Even small power outages reveal our patience.
Cooking on gas becomes an art.
You have to laugh and enjoy the moment.

bell: The bell rang, and two minutes later the power went out.
This town has always had a sense of humour.
Still — nobody minded the dark last night.

name: Busisiwe
dialog: Hearing different languages on the wind is beautiful.
They connect people, even strangers.
Our town has many voices waiting to be heard.

name: Sibusiso
dialog: The taxis are the heartbeat of our town.
Without them, the coast is silent.
Finding lost signs keeps life moving smoothly.
postQuestDialog: You recovered the missing route sign?
Drivers won’t argue at the harbor anymore.
You’ve kept the rhythm of the town alive.

quest.description: Locate the missing taxi route sign to help the early commuters navigate the coastal roads.

name: Palesa
dialog: Spring here paints the cliffs in gold and violet.
The wildflowers sway with the breeze.
It’s like walking through a living painting.

name: Andile
dialog: Soccer brings the town together.
Even the seagulls pause when the ball rolls by.
It’s chaos, laughter, and cheers in one field.

name: Kgotso
dialog: Evenings on the cliffs are calm.
Watching the sun set over the waves is enough for reflection.
Peace lives here if you stop and look.

fragments: So you're the one asking about the bell.
Nandi said someone she trusts was doing the looking.

name: Nandi
dialog: Some nights, when the fog rolls in, I hear a bell.
Not from the harbor — from somewhere deeper.
People say it’s just the sea, but it feels… intentional.
postQuestDialog: You found something, didn’t you?
That sound… it wasn’t just in my head.
Maybe the town is trying to remember.
I've heard that Kagiso may know more.
epilogueDialog: You heard it too, right? The whole town did.
They rang it for the ones who didn’t come home.
This time it rang for one who did.

quest.description: Search the shoreline and forest edge for traces of the bell.
quest.unlockText: The fragments are real. Nandi wasn't imagining it. Kagiso, they say, remembers what the bell was for.

name: Themba
dialog: Driving along winding coastal roads teaches focus.
Every turn matters, every view is a reward.
City driving feels easy after this.
Mind the potholes, though. The municipality stopped counting them years ago.
postQuestDialog: You sent the photos in?
The roads desk says they'll 'schedule an assessment'.
So — next year, maybe. But it's on record now.
That's how things start moving around here.

quest.description: Photograph 4 of the worst potholes for the municipality's roads desk.

name: Ayanda
dialog: Elder stories whisper lessons without lectures.
Along the cliffs, the wind carries them far.
You remember them long after you hear them.

name: Mandla
dialog: Strength is more than muscle.
Enduring challenges along the coast builds resilience.
Our town teaches it quietly to everyone.

name: Noluthando
dialog: Kindness travels further than the tides.
A smile or greeting brightens the busiest street.
Ubuntu is alive here, if you care to see it.

name: Hlokomela
dialog: No one walks up there anymore.
Paths don’t vanish on their own.
They disappear when people stop caring.
I sweep the bottom steps out of habit. Someone keeps sweeping the top ones.

bell: Both sets of steps were swept.

postQuestDialog: The path feels open again.
Like it’s breathing.
Thank you for that.
I've heard that the lighthouse keeper may know more.

quest.description: Restore the forgotten markers leading to the lighthouse.
quest.unlockText: The path to the lighthouse is open. Someone is still up there.

name: Thandi
dialog: Early mornings along the coast are quiet.
The town wakes with the sunrise and the waves.
Notice the little details others miss.

path: There was a light at the point this morning. Just for a moment, before sunrise.
I don't think I imagined it.

name: Refilwe
dialog: The park along the cliffs is forgotten lately.
Litter dulls its beauty.
Even small actions can bring life back.
postQuestDialog: You picked up the litter?
The park already feels lighter and alive.
Thank you for caring.
You know… Bongani has been fussing over that broken street light for weeks. Maybe you're the one to help him.

quest.description: Collect 5 pieces of litter scattered along the park pathways and cliff edge.
quest.unlockText: Refilwe mentioned Bongani, still fussing over a broken street light on the promenade.

name: Bongani
dialog: Broken street lights make the town feel shadowed.
This one hasn’t worked for weeks.
Someone needs to restore it for night safety.
postQuestDialog: You fixed the street light?
Even one light changes how safe the streets feel.
The town thanks you.
Now the children will play out later — though Keabetswe says their balls keep vanishing into the tide.

quest.description: Inspect and restore the broken street light along the coastal promenade.
quest.unlockText: Bongani says the children near Keabetswe's stall keep losing their play balls.

name: Keabetswe
dialog: The children lost their play balls again. They roll down the streets, some nearly to the tide line.
If you spot any on your rounds, gather them up.
Leave them at the soccer pitch — that's where the game is.
postQuestDialog: The balls are back at the pitch?
The kids are already down there playing.
You’ve made their day.
If only everyone knew how the promenade is coming back to life… Mpho's community board could tell them, if it weren't bare.

quest.description: Round up 3 play balls from the streets and drop them off at the soccer pitch.
quest.unlockText: Keabetswe thinks Mpho could spread the good news — if the community board weren't empty.

name: Samkelo
dialog: Vendors along the coast rely on foot traffic.
Signs guide visitors, but mine blew away last night.
Without it, customers get lost.
postQuestDialog: Your sign is back!
People can find your stall again.
The morning feels busy and happy once more.

quest.description: Recover the missing vendor sign along the coastal market street.

name: Mpho
dialog: The community board shares news for the town.
Lately, few check it.
Missing notices mean missed opportunities.
postQuestDialog: You put the notices back up?
Everyone can see them again.
It’s amazing how much that matters.
A clean park, a bright light, laughing children, and news worth reading… tonight, the promenade celebrates. You made this happen.

quest.description: Post 3 missing community notices along the promenade and market square.

name: Lighthouse Keeper
dialog: So. Someone finally followed the sound.
I know your face. You stand the way your sister does — like you're already halfway to the next place.
I kept the light long after the town stopped looking up.
The rope rotted in '09. The winch seized the year after. I kept the ledger anyway — every boat out, every safe return.
The old bell needs attention… find it, and let them hear it one more time.
postQuestDialog: You hear that? The whole bay heard it.
A town that hears its bell again starts to remember itself.
Thank you, courier. The light is yours now too.

quest.description: Restore the old warning bell at the lighthouse.
